newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Bildt seen leaving Bosnia in May.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Bildt seen leaving Bosnia in May.

text.p: Carl Bildt, the leader of Sweden's main opposition party who is overseeing peace efforts in Bosnia, is likely to return to Sweden for good in May, a spokesman said on Tuesday.

Bildt, in hospital in Stockholm with a suspected viral infection, has said he will leave Bosnia this year and return to Sweden to prepare the conservative Moderate Party for the general election in September 1998.
"He will come before the summer, some time in May seems likely," the Moderates' press secretary Jacob Broberg said.
Bildt, 47, was admitted on Saturday with a suspected viral infection after collapsing at home. He had headaches and difficulty speaking but his condition is not considered serious.
Bildt was prime minister from 1991 to 1994 when the Moderates lost power to the Social Democrats in polls.
After the election defeat, he took on the Bosnian mission, where he is now the major powers' High Representative.

In the latest opinion poll by the Swedish Institute of Public Opinion and Research (SIFO), published on Sunday, the Moderates gained 30.9 percent of the vote compared to the ruling Social Democrats 29.1 percent.
This was the second consecutive poll that has shown the Moderates to be ahead of the Social Democrats.
